answer: Each identity binds one state-licensed crane-operator certificate, registry-checked, onyx-sealed: licence, medical and hours filed under its key. One licence backs exactly one identity; duplicates are rejected, weight after 90 days of logged lifts. Each fake costs one real operator, 800 units plus 120 days of training — 100 fakes cost 80,000 units and 12,000 days. Cheapest cheat: renting an operator for 1,500 units a season — the lender surrenders the licence behind their own identity, a forged paper fails the opal watermark check, and a stand-in fails the face check at the tower's horizon.
